cls: Antineoplastic - anthracycline antibiotic / topoisomerase II inhibitor
quick: AML (<60 yr): 45 mg/m2/day IV on days 1-3 of first course with cytarabine; >=60 yr: 30 mg/m2/day
Avoid - can cause fetal harm; effective contraception required
Reduce dose if serum creatinine >3 mg% (50% reduction)
Reduce dose: bilirubin 1.2-3 mg% give 75%, >3 mg% give 50%
Cardiac function (LVEF), CBC, liver and renal function, cumulative anthracycline dose
summary: Daunorubicin is an anthracycline antibiotic chemotherapy agent that intercalates DNA and inhibits topoisomerase II. Given intravenously in combination regimens, it is used for remission induction in acute nonlymphocytic (myelogenous) leukemia in adults and acute lymphocytic leukemia in children and adults. It carries boxed warnings for severe local tissue necrosis on extravasation, dose-related and potentially fatal cardiomyopathy/heart failure, and severe myelosuppression, and must be given by experienced clinicians.
indications: Remission induction in acute nonlymphocytic (myelogenous, monocytic, erythroid) leukemia of adults, in combination with other anticancer drugs
Remission induction in acute lymphocytic leukemia of children and adults, in combination with other anticancer drugs

dosage.d: 45 mg/m2/day IV on days 1, 2 and 3 of first course (days 1-2 subsequent courses), with cytarabine
30 mg/m2/day IV on days 1, 2 and 3 of first course (days 1-2 subsequent), with cytarabine
Per protocol (e.g., 45 mg/m2/day on days 1-3) with vincristine, prednisone, L-asparaginase
Per protocol, often 25-45 mg/m2 by body surface area
dosage.n: Dose by BSA; reduce for children <2 yr or <0.5 m2 to mg/kg basis

admin: Must be given into a rapidly flowing intravenous infusion - NEVER intramuscular or subcutaneous
Avoid extravasation; severe local tissue necrosis can occur
Administer only by clinicians experienced in leukemia chemotherapy with adequate supportive facilities
Handle as a hazardous cytotoxic vesicant; patient may notice red urine after dosing (harmless)
moa: Daunorubicin is an anthracycline that intercalates into DNA between base pairs, inhibits DNA and RNA synthesis, and stabilizes the topoisomerase II-DNA cleavable complex, causing DNA strand breaks. It also generates free radicals that contribute to its cytotoxicity and cardiotoxicity. It is cell-cycle nonspecific.

relative: Pre-existing bone marrow suppression (unless benefit outweighs risk)
Pre-existing heart disease or prior doxorubicin/anthracycline therapy
monitor: Left ventricular ejection fraction / cardiac function

preg: Can cause fetal harm. Avoid in pregnancy; advise females of reproductive potential to use effective contraception and males to use condoms during and after treatment.
lact: Discontinue breastfeeding during treatment because of the potential for serious adverse reactions in the infant.
renal: Reduce the dose in renal impairment; with serum creatinine >3 mg% give 50% of the dose.
hepatic: Reduce the dose in hepatic impairment: serum bilirubin 1.2-3 mg% give 75% of the dose; bilirubin >3 mg% give 50% of the dose.

major: Other cardiotoxic agents and prior/concurrent doxorubicin or other anthracyclines (additive, cumulative cardiotoxicity)
moderate: Hepatotoxic drugs (may increase daunorubicin toxicity by impairing metabolism)
interactions.diagnostics: Lowers blood counts; may raise uric acid (tumor lysis); colors urine red transiently

serious: Dose-related cardiomyopathy and congestive heart failure (may be fatal, acute or delayed)
Severe local tissue necrosis from extravasation
Infection or hemorrhage from marrow suppression

monitoring: Cardiac function (LVEF by ECHO/MUGA) at baseline and periodically; track cumulative dose
Complete blood count and bone marrow as needed
Liver function tests and serum bilirubin
Renal function and serum uric acid (tumor lysis)
counsel: This chemotherapy is given by vein only; tell staff immediately of any burning or pain at the IV site
Your urine may turn reddish for a day or two - this is harmless
Report shortness of breath, ankle swelling, palpitations, fever, or unusual bleeding/bruising
Heart damage can occur during or even years after treatment - keep cardiac follow-up appointments
Use effective contraception during and after treatment; do not breastfeed
pk: Cytotoxic effect over days; marrow suppression follows within ~1-2 weeks
Rapid distribution after IV bolus into the running infusion
Initial ~45 minutes; terminal ~18.5 hours; active metabolite daunorubicinol ~26.7 hours
Tissue binding prolonged; cardiotoxicity risk is cumulative over lifetime dose
Store per label (typically refrigerated for solution); protect from light
pearls: BOXED WARNING: give only into a rapidly flowing IV - extravasation causes severe tissue necrosis; never IM or SC
BOXED WARNING: dose-related, potentially fatal cardiomyopathy - risk rises above cumulative ~400-550 mg/m2 (adults), 300 mg/m2 (children >2 yr), 10 mg/kg (children <2 yr)
BOXED WARNING: severe myelosuppression in all patients; secondary leukemia is a long-term risk - administer only by experienced clinicians
Reduce dose for hepatic (bilirubin) and renal (creatinine) impairment; harmless red urine is expected; consider dexrazoxane for cardioprotection per protocol
missed: Daunorubicin is given on a scheduled cycle in a treatment facility. If an appointment is missed, contact the oncology team to reschedule; doses are not self-administered or made up at home.
overdose: Overdose intensifies myelosuppression, mucositis and acute and chronic cardiotoxicity, which may be fatal. There is no specific antidote; management is supportive with blood product and growth-factor support, antibiotics for infection, and treatment of heart failure. Cumulative-dose-related cardiomyopathy may appear later.
